<!--
Chains onto usgs_elevation_and_z_star.qmd's output -- reads
usgs_elev_z_flux.csv (elevation already joined) and adds veg on top,
so both covariates are present before the Bay/River split, matching
elevation's "join before tier" position. Writes
usgs_elev_veg_flux_long.csv.

THIS FILE'S OUTPUT IS NOT AN INPUT TO master_analysis_usgs.Rmd's
sed_usgs / tiering, BY DESIGN, PERMANENTLY -- see the note in that
file's "read back" chunk. Multi-species fan-out means this table has
more rows than one-per-flux-observation; it exists as its own parallel
object for species-level visualization, not as a replacement for
usgs_elev_z_flux.csv in the core pipeline.

Cleaning logic below reuses the pattern already in veg.Rmd's usgs_veg
chunk (NA -> 0 for AvgHt/MaxHt, whitespace stripping, Cover as numeric)
-- not reinvented, just relocated into the pipeline and adapted for
column-name specifics found in the actual uploaded CSV (trailing space
in "Month " and "Season", ALL CAPS month names, no Replicate column).

MULTI-SPECIES ROWS KEPT INTENTIONALLY, CONFIRMED: usgs_SFB_1m_vegetation_data.csv
has multiple species rows at the same Site+Plot+Month+Year (up to 3 --
e.g. San Pablo C24 in July 2023 has SAPA, SPFO, and a third species all
logged separately). This is by design, for per-species visualization
(the SAPA_usgs/SPFO_usgs-style breakdowns already in veg.Rmd), not
something to collapse. "_long" in the filename means "one row per
species per flux observation, by design."

CONSEQUENCE THAT STILL MATTERS: any Flux-based aggregate (mean flux,
tier statistics, a Flux ~ ... model) computed directly on this
long-form table will double- or triple-count Flux at multi-species
plots. Fine for species-level visualization; not fine for anything
summarizing or modeling Flux without filtering to one species first.
-->

```{r, load packages}
source("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\code\\R\\setup.R")
```

```{r, load elevation-joined flux data and raw veg data}
# Reads the elevation join's output, not master_usgs.csv directly --
# this is the chained step, elevation then veg, both before tiering.
usgs_elev_z_flux <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\usgs_elev_z_flux.csv")

usgs_veg_raw <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\usgs_SFB_1m_vegetation_data.csv")
```

```{r, clean usgs veg -- same pattern as veg.Rmd's usgs_veg chunk}
usgs_veg <- usgs_veg_raw |>
  rename(Month = `Month.`) |>   # trailing space in the raw column name
  mutate(
    AvgHt   = ifelse(is.na(AvgHt), 0, AvgHt),
    MaxHt   = ifelse(is.na(MaxHt), 0, MaxHt),
    Cover   = as.numeric(Cover),
    Season  = str_squish(Season),
    Site    = str_remove_all(Site, " "),                 # "Corte Madera" -> "CorteMadera", matches master_usgs.csv
    Year    = str_squish(as.character(Year)),
    Month   = str_to_title(str_squish(Month)),            # "AUGUST" -> "August", matches master_usgs.csv's Month
    Tran    = str_extract(`Plot.ID`, "^[A-Za-z]+"),
    Dist    = as.numeric(str_extract(`Plot.ID`, "[0-9.]+$"))
  )

str(usgs_veg)

# Confirms the fan-out risk flagged above, before it hits the join --
# any Site+Tran+Dist+Month+Year with n > 1 has multiple species logged.
usgs_veg |>
  count(Site, Tran, Dist, Month, Year) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  nrow()
```

```{r, key the flux data to match}
usgs_flux_keyed <- usgs_elev_z_flux |>
  mutate(
    Site  = str_squish(as.character(Site)),
    Tran  = str_squish(as.character(Tran)),
    Dist  = as.numeric(as.character(Dist)),
    Month = str_squish(as.character(Month)),
    Year  = str_squish(as.character(Year))
  )
```

```{r, join -- long form, species not collapsed}
# 5-key join (Site, Tran, Dist, Month, Year -- no Replicate, same
# broadcast logic as elevation, but now also time-matched since veg
# was only sampled 3 times rather than being a static survey).
usgs_elev_veg_flux_long <- usgs_flux_keyed |>
  left_join(
    usgs_veg |> select(Site, Tran, Dist, Month, Year, Species, AvgHt, MaxHt, Cover),
    by = c("Site", "Tran", "Dist", "Month", "Year")
  )

readr::write_csv(usgs_elev_veg_flux_long, "C:\\Users\\savan\\OneDrive - San Francisco State University\\ProjectData\\GitHub\\DepositionSFB\\data\\usgs_elev_veg_flux_long.csv")
```

```{r, diagnostics -- shows the fan-out and the temporal sparsity, fixes nothing}
# Row count BEFORE this join (should equal nrow(usgs_flux_keyed) if
# every flux row matched at most one veg row -- it won't, because of
# the multi-species fan-out, which is intentional -- see header note).
nrow(usgs_flux_keyed)
nrow(usgs_elev_veg_flux_long)
nrow(usgs_elev_veg_flux_long) - nrow(usgs_flux_keyed)   # rows added by species fan-out, expected and fine here

# How many distinct flux observations (not species-rows) actually got
# ANY veg match at all -- expected to be small, since veg was only
# sampled in 3 of the 16 Month/Year windows the flux data spans.
usgs_flux_keyed |>
  left_join(
    usgs_veg |> distinct(Site, Tran, Dist, Month, Year) |> mutate(has_veg = TRUE),
    by = c("Site", "Tran", "Dist", "Month", "Year")
  ) |>
  count(has_veg)
```
